transcript.text: Is it normal that I can hear water running in my washer dryer the whole time it's DRYING? Worried it's leaking or costing me a fortune on the water meter.

It is very likely normal. Most condenser tumble dryers and washer-dryers pump cold water through a heat exchanger to cool down the hot air during the drying cycle; this creates a running sound but uses only a small amount of water (usually 1–2 litres per load). However, to rule out a fault like a stuck inlet valve or siphoning, please check two things: is there any water pooling on the floor around the machine? And if you turn the water tap off at the wall while it is drying, does the noise stop immediately?

No water on the floor, I checked with kitchen roll and it's dry. I haven't tried turning the tap off at the wall - should I do that while it's mid-cycle? Also no burning smell, just a warm laundry smell.

[Heading: Normal condenser cooling operation]
That is excellent news regarding the floor and smell; it strongly suggests there is no leak or overheating fault. The sound you are hearing is almost certainly the machine pumping cold water through its condenser to cool down the hot air during drying—this is normal operation for a condenser washer-dryer. To confirm this definitively, please turn the water tap off at the wall while it is mid-cycle. If the noise stops immediately, it confirms the machine is using water as part of the cooling process and there is no leak or siphoning issue. You can then safely leave the tap on for future loads.

Ok, I'll try turning the tap off mid-cycle. Is it fine for the machine to run a drying cycle without water for a bit? I'd rather not damage it. I also hear the drain pump come on every few minutes during drying, if that matters.

[Heading: Normal operation]
Yes, it is perfectly safe to run the drying cycle without water for a short time; the machine will simply cool down slightly slower until the tap is turned back on. The intermittent drain pump noise you hear is also normal: as cold water flows through the condenser to cool the hot air, it picks up heat and creates steam/warm condensate that needs to be pumped away periodically. Since there are no leaks on the floor and no burning smells, your machine is behaving exactly as designed for a condenser washer-dryer.
